summary: Shun'ei Matsushita worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University, serving as a fixed-term assistant professor until 2013 and as a part-time lecturer attested in 2017.
Shun'ei Mori worked in Buddhist studies and studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held an appointment as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College, attested in 1995.
Shunei Tsuboi (1921–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Bukkyo University, attested in 1963 and 1972.

Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held a post at Toyo University and served at Taisho University from circa 1943 to 1980, becoming professor emeritus.
Shunpaku Nakao worked in Buddhist studies, serving at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1963) and later as a professor (attested 1976).

Shunpei Ueyama (1921–2012) studied philosophy and Japanology at Taihoku High School and Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University (1954–1984), and later served as director of Kyoto National Museum (~1991–1995) and president of Kyoto City University of Arts (~1995–1999).

Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji under several traditional teachers. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Soko-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

Shunsho Manabe (1939–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology, studying at Tohoku University (~1958–1963). He held posts at Hosen Gakuen College (~1994–2003) and Shikoku University (~2003–2017), where he was a professor.
Shunsho Terakawa (1928–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served at Otani University from circa 1968 to 2000, where he became emeritus professor.

Shunsuke Tsurumi (1922–2015) studied philosophy at Harvard University (~1939–1942) under Willard Van Orman Quine. He held posts at Kyoto University (~1949–1954), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1954–1960), and Doshisha University (~1960–1970).

Shuntaro Kondo (b. 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD from Ryukoku University by 2011. He was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University in 2012.

Shuntarō Matsuyama (1930–2014) studied Indology and religious studies at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji. He was a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (attested 1994) and lectured at Kokugakuin, Tama Art University, and Bigakko.

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a D.Lit. from Bukkyo University by 1993. He served at Bukkyo University as an associate professor (attested 1996) and later as a professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka (1927–2009) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He served as an assistant professor at Toyo University from circa 1961 to 1992.
Shuyu Sakurai (b. 1916) worked in Buddhist studies, graduating from Tohoku University (~1940–1943). He held a post at Komazawa University (~1950–1987), where he became professor emeritus.

Shwe Zan Aung (1871–1932) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon (~1888–1891) and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.
Shōdō Yamagami (b. 1939) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University (~1962–1964). He served as an assistant professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from circa 1971 to 2008.
Shōkō Kabutogi (1912–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1933–1936). He later served there as a professor from circa 1958 to 1982.

Si Ti La works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Acharya Nagarjuna University under doctoral supervisor J. Sitaramamma, having also studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala, U Sajjanasara, and Sayadaw U Sasana.

Sibani Dasgupta worked in Indology, studying at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.
